focus: TitanDiet.cs: FoodIsSuitable postfix semantics vs vanilla CanEverEat, IsPotentiallyPredator, BestFoodSourceOnMap plant fallback, JobGiver_GetFood postfix hunger gate, JobDriver_TitanEatNonFood (reservations, stack counts, nutrition), Diet cache invalidation in Hediff_Titan, hot-path cost
diffSource: since build 44 (2026-10-07T03:15:43Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Plant fallback in BestFoodSourceOnMap postfix ignores the rope check
findings.detail: Vanilla's foodValidator rejects a food source more than 8 cells from a roped getter's anchor (`getter.roping.IsRoped` / `InHorDistOf(RopedTo.Cell, 8f)`). The fallback's validator (`t is Plant && t.IngestibleNow && eater.WillEat(t, getter) && ... && getter.CanReserve(t)`) has no such check, so a roped titan whose diet adds plants can be sent to a far plant. Add `(!getter.roping.IsRoped || t.PositionHeld.InHorDistOf(getter.roping.RopedTo.Cell, 8f))` to that lambda. The same gap is in EatNonFoodJob's validator.

findings.title: EatNonFoodJob runs an uncapped whole-map search per non-food def on every failed GetFood
findings.detail: Each entry in d.nonFood gets its own GenClosest.ClosestThingReachable with no searchRegionsMax, and the JobGiver_GetFood postfix calls it every time vanilla finds no food, which for a hungry titan with nothing to eat can be every think cycle. The rockgut example has five defs. Vanilla limits the same kind of search with FoodUtility.GetMaxRegionsToScan(getter, forceScanWholeMap); pass that as searchRegionsMax in the ClosestThingReachable call in EatNonFoodJob.

findings.title: Diet-added foods skip willNeverEat and the mutant food-type override
findings.detail: When vanilla returns false, the postfix sets ok=true for any food d.Adds() accepts, after checking only EatsFood, preferability and babiesCanIngest. Vanilla's other refusals, RaceProperties.willNeverEat and a mutant's own food type (overrideFoodType), are overridden for added foods. That is probably intended, but it is not 'on top of its race' for those two cases.

findings.title: refuseFoods is not honoured on paths that skip FoodIsSuitable
findings.detail: JobGiver_EatRandom checks RaceProps.CanEverEat directly, and JobDriver_PredatorHunt eats its kill through Toils_Ingest with no WillEat check. A trait that refuses Corpse but has hunts=true still eats what it kills. Build() does set hunts=false when Corpse is removed and hunts is unset, but an explicit hunts=true overrides that, and ConfigErrors does not warn about the combination.

findings.title: Material eating is on by default for every existing material titan, wild ones included
findings.detail: materialNutritionPerUnit defaults to 0.05, so TitanDiet.Build gives every titan whose material isn't food a nonFood entry. Existing saves' gold, jade and plasteel titans will eat stockpiled material once they have no other food. The settings hint says 'Tamed ones eat from your stockpiles unless the stack is forbidden', but IsForbidden is always false for factionless pawns, so wild titans do it too.

findings.title: FoodIsSuitable postfix adds a registry lookup to every food check
findings.detail: PeekTitan does a ConditionalWeakTable TryGetValue for every pawn, and a hediffs.Contains for titans, once per candidate food item in every food search on the map. That is cheap per call, but it is now on the hottest path in food search. This is an opinion; it was not measured.
